newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No cold in sight for Brazil coffee regions - Somar.
newsitem.headline: No cold in sight for Brazil coffee regions - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions face no risk of damaging cold in the next five days, with any polar air masses all passing through the far south of the country, local meteorologists Somar said on Thursday.
A cold front is bringing cloudy weather and isolated showers to producing areas in the north of Parana and southwest of Sao Paulo states, Somar said.
In the south and Cerrado regions of Minas Gerais and in the north of Sao Paulo, mainly sunny weather is forecast with some light cloud.
Minimum temperatures should remain between 10 and 17 degrees Celsius, Somar said.
The latest models continue to show the development of the El Nino weather phenomenon in the Pacific Ocean which is keeping cold fronts blocked in the south of Brazil.
As a result, temperatures are above the seasonal average in the southeast region where coffee is grown, Somar said.
